core_result: A single explicit radial log-concave density family eventually makes P(-partial)p positive if and only if a finite Hermitian polynomial P with P(0)>0 is positive definite on every real point.
classical_dependency: Strict Krivine-Stengle Positivstellensatz applied to det P gives an algebraic lower margin; finite Bell expansion gives uniform relative error.
sharpening: Density shape is independent of the polynomial and its margin function. Sufficient broadening still depends on acquired margin and coefficient bounds.
sharp_example: For Q(s,t)=(st-1)^2+s^2 and the stated radial power-potential family, beta<=1/5 is sufficient after broadening and beta>1/5 fails for every scale. Sharp exponent 6/5 only in that family.
counterexamples: Every nondegenerate Gaussian fails for the strictly positive sum of squares Q.
A degree-two diagonal bounded-operator polynomial is coercive at every real point but defeats every scale of the canonical logarithmic density family.
Free commutator information is erased by commuting differential variables.
A positive chosen differential output does not imply a positive Green inverse.
validation: Five exact symbolic identity checks, one exact matrix counterexample, and finite high-precision diagnostics pass; not formal verification or global numerical certification.
